def test():
    import jobs
    # Test basic deduplication by (source, source_id)
    rows = [
        {'title': 'A', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': 's1'},
        {'title': 'B', 'source': 'src2', 'source_id': 's1'},
        {'title': 'C', 'source': 'src3', 'source_id': 's1'},
        {'title': 'A', 'source': 'src4', 'source_id': 's1'},  # Same title, different source
    ]
    result = jobs.unique_jobs(rows)
    assert len(result) == 4, f"Expected 4 rows, got {len(result)}: {result}"

    # Test that same source with different ids are separate
    rows2 = [
        {'title': 'X', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': 'i1'},
        {'title': 'Y', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': 'i2'},
    ]
    result2 = jobs.unique_jobs(rows2)
    assert len(result2) == 2, f"Expected 2 rows, got {len(result2)}: {result2}"

    # Test that different sources are not merged
    rows3 = [
        {'title': 'Job', 'source': 'alpha', 'source_id': '123'},
        {'title': 'Job', 'source': 'beta', 'source_id': '123'},
    ]
    result3 = jobs.unique_jobs(rows3)
    assert len(result3) == 2, f"Expected 2 rows, got {len(result3)}: {result3}"

    # Test that None/empty source_id keeps row separately
    rows4 = [
        {'title': 'X', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': 'a'},
        {'title': 'Y', 'source': 'src2', 'source_id': ''},
        {'title': 'Z', 'source': 'src3', 'source_id': None},
    ]
    result4 = jobs.unique_jobs(rows4)
    assert len(result4) == 3, f"Expected 3 rows, got {len(result4)}: {result4}"

    # Test that (source, '') and (source, None) are different keys
    rows5 = [
        {'title': 'A', 'source': 's1', 'source_id': ''},
        {'title': 'B', 'source': 's1', 'source_id': None},
    ]
    result5 = jobs.unique_jobs(rows5)
    assert len(result5) == 2, f"Expected 2 rows, got {len(result5)}: {result5}"

    print("All tests passed!")
